# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible canonical-fitting rival is **`rank_cap_5`**: apply the
intended row rule, except never place the color-6 anchor later than position 5
(zero-based) inside the reconstructed bar. Equivalently, use
`min(actual_non7_rank, 5)` as the anchor rank. This fits all three canonical
input/output pairs because their largest color-6 rank among non-7 cells is 5.

An exact lawful disagreement input is:

```json
[
  [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
  [7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7],
  [7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7],
  [7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7],
  [7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7],
  [7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7]
]
```

The active row has seven non-7 cells and the 6 has rank 6. The intended output
row is `[8,8,8,8,8,8,8,7]`; `rank_cap_5` instead predicts
`[7,8,8,8,8,8,8,8]`. They differ at `(0,0)` and `(0,7)`.

I checked the intended output with the supported canonical Racket runner:

```text
cwd: WORK/repo
arcpuzzles apply 587396c0817d \
  --input generators/587396c0817d/counterexamples/rank-cap-5/input.json \
  --out ../checks/rank-cap-5-racket.json
```

The retained receipt reports executed rule hash `703072e0ab28`, final generator
SHA-256 `c5c8f3618a62ad81eabb7fb95461fc1fd2eae5242417c3cd8e22a86448d719e8`,
and exactly the intended output above. The full input, Racket output, rival
output, hashes, and differing cells are in
`repo/generators/587396c0817d/counterexamples/rank-cap-5/counterexample.json`.

**Yes, the repaired generator emits such cases.** Every default
`rank_six_witness` profile forces that decisive row, and the period-2 schedule
places this profile at every even `sample_index`. With three demonstrations,
every four-pair production window has two such witnesses, so any single query
rotation leaves at least one in the demonstrations. Explicit overrides bypass
the curriculum schedule by design.
